title: add jsonschema strict response_format + improved validation errors
author: Priya Kapoor
description:
Context: Add a first-class response_format option that supports json_schema with a strict mode. Motivation: customers are using structured output heavily (tooling, ingestion pipelines) and minor deviations from schemas cause downstream failures. This PR introduces a response_format=json_schema (existing) and a new parameter strict=true|false that enforces deterministic validation behavior and clearer error messages. Summary of changes:
- Add response_format field parsing in API surface and OpenAI-compatible layer (redwood-openai-compat).
- Implement strict schema validation path in the request pipeline: when strict=true, parser returns 400 with structured validation errors and does not attempt best-effort repairs. When strict=false (default), we preserve current best-effort repair logic and return warnings in response metadata.
- Improve validation error messages to include: JSON Pointer to failing field, expected schema type/format, sample corrective suggestion, and whether the field is required or additional.
- Update streaming logic to emit schema-violation markers in-stream (+ final metadata) instead of silent repairs, to aid client-side tooling and streaming consumers.
- Add unit/integration tests for strict mode, streaming violation markers, OpenAI compat endpoints, and SDK surface.
- Docs and changelog entries.
Checklist:
- [x] API surface changes + param parsing
- [x] Runtime validation + strict enforcement
- [x] Streaming markers + final validation metadata
- [x] Error message improvements and i18n key placeholders
- [x] Tests (unit + integ)
- [x] Docs + release notes
Commits (high level):
- feat(api): add response_format parsing and new strict flag
- feat(runtime): add strict schema validation path and error types
- feat(streaming): emit schema_violation events in streaming protocol
- fix(compat): map OpenAI response_format param to internal response_format
- test: add tests for strict mode and streaming behavior
- docs: add jsonschema strict mode section and examples
CI: initial CI run failed due to a lint rule (unused import) and a flaky integ test. Lint fix pushed; integ test was flaky in the batching harness and was made deterministic by seeding rng in test. Final CI: pass.
Review conversation (summary):
- Miguel Santos (reviewer): asked for clearer error payload shape and example client handling flow; requested that strict mode be opt-in. Author reply: agreed, made default strict=false and documented migration guidance.
- Helena Park (security): asked whether strict mode could cause data exposure in error messages. Author: ensured error payload omits sensitive prompt content and uses JSON Pointer references only.
- Aaron Feldman (runtime): requested microbenchmark for latency impact of strict validation on 8k flows; author: added a small benchmark and added an opt-out header for latency-sensitive routes.
- Approvals: Miguel Santos (approved), Helena Park (approved), Aaron Feldman (approved after perf bench).
Merge: squash and merge.
Release notes:
- Add response_format=json_schema with strict=true option to enforce exact schema compliance. When strict=true, requests failing validation return 400 with structured validation errors. Default behavior remains best-effort with warnings. See docs/reference/response_format.md for examples and migration guidance.

examples_in_description: Example: request body: {"response_format": {"type": "json_schema", "schema": {...}, "strict": true}} -> when validation fails returns 400 and body: {"error": {"type": "schema_validation_error", "errors": [{"pointer": "/user/email", "expected": "email", "message": "invalid email format", "suggestion": "use a valid email like user@example.com"}]}}
notes: This PR touches the OpenAI compatibility layer to preserve parity with the openai-like response_format param. Added migration docs and a short perf note about an opt-out header for low-latency paths. Flaky integ test was stabilized by seeding.
